title: Predicting a Sound Before Finding Its Letters — Saussure's 1878 Coefficients Sonantiques, Hrozný & Kuryłowicz's Hittite Laryngeals (ḫ) & Internal Reconstruction

teenKit.tldr: A 21-year-old linguistics student used pure math and logic in 1879 to predict an ancient consonant sound decades before archaeologists actually dug up clay tablets proving it existed. It is the linguistic equivalent of predicting a black hole before seeing it.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It proves that human reason can reverse-engineer deep history and uncover hidden truths about how our ancestors spoke and thought, long before any written records were found.
keyTakeaways: Ferdinand de Saussure used structural logic and pattern recognition to deduce the existence of a missing vowel-altering sound (a 'coefficient sonantique') without a single piece of physical text.
Decades later, the decipherment of Hittite clay tablets by Friedrich Hrozný physically proved that Saussure's invisible sound (the laryngeal consonant ḫ) was real all along.
Internal reconstruction is a detective method linguists use to wind language backward in time, finding hidden rules by analyzing weird patterns and irregularities in modern or historical words.

vocab.meaning: Saussure's theoretical placeholder name for a phantom sound that he mathematically proved must have existed in prehistoric Indo-European.
A harsh consonant sound made deep in the throat, like the 'ch' in the Scottish word 'loch' or the German 'Bach'.
A linguistic detective technique that reverse-engineers older ancestral language rules by studying odd exceptions and irregularities in a single later language.
An ancient, long-forgotten Anatolian civilization whose clay tablets finally provided physical evidence of Saussure's predicted sounds.

quiz.question: How did Ferdinand de Saussure first discover the missing sound in 1879?
options: By unearthing a dusty clay tablet in his basement
By using pure mathematical and structural logic to spot gaps in word patterns
By listening to isolated remote tribes in the Amazon
By using early audio recording devices to capture ancient dialects
quiz.explanation: Saussure didn't have physical artifacts; he deduced the missing sound entirely through structural linguistic logic.

quiz.question: What is the primary purpose of 'internal reconstruction' in historical linguistics?
options: To translate modern slang into ancient Greek
To rebuild broken pieces of physical pottery found at archaeological sites
To reverse-engineer older forms of a language by analyzing its current weird patterns and exceptions
To predict what languages will sound like a thousand years in the future
quiz.explanation: Internal reconstruction uses current irregularities and rule exceptions as clues to wind a language's history backward.

quiz.question: How was Saussure's theoretical prediction ultimately validated decades later?
options: By modern DNA sequencing of ancient human remains
Through the decipherment of Hittite cuneiform tablets containing the exact predicted sounds
By discovering a living tribe that still spoke unmodified Proto-Indo-European
quiz.explanation: Friedrich Hrozný deciphered Hittite texts that literally spelled out the laryngeal consonants Saussure had predicted.
